inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense (10-K cash flow statement add-back), FY2025 = $13.8M. No separate equity-award-tax-withholding cash tag is disclosed by AOS (SharesPaidForTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation is a share count, not a cash figure); SBC is immaterial here (0.36% of FY2025 revenue) versus a SaaS issuer, so the omission is not consequential.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% built on a US industrial: ~4.2% 10Y Treasury + ~4.3pp ERP-adjusted beta premium (AOS beta ~1.1-1.2, moderately cyclical replacement-demand manufacturer with a small China/tariff overlay). Held flat across scenarios per section 7f (risk is charged once, in the scenario cash flows, not stacked onto WACC).
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- AOS does not disclose a material operating-lease asset/liability separate from ordinary trade facilities; no lease adjustment applied.
inputs.notes: Route: owner-FCF DCF (SKILL.md routing table row 1/2 -- ordinary US industrial operating company; no adaptations file needed, no NCI, no dual currency, no material leases). CAPEX WAS NOT IN THE PARSED XBRL/CSV (CapEx and FreeCashFlow columns are NULL for every period; the dcf-context tool's 'free_cash_flow' column silently fell back to raw OperatingCashFlow because both CapEx and FCF were null in metrics_normalized -- this understated the true capex deduction by the full capex amount and must not be read as FCF). CapEx was recovered directly from SEC XBRL companyconcept CIK0000091142/us-gaap/PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets -- AOS files this non-standard capex tag instead of the common PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment tag, which is why the generic parser found nothing. FY2025 capex = $70.8M (1.85% of revenue), in line with FY2020-2023 (1.87-2.12%); FY2024's $108.0M (2.83%) was a one-off capacity-investment year and is treated as such, not carried forward. Reported FCF = OCF $616.8M - CapEx $70.8M = $546.0M (this is inputs.reported_fcf); owner FCF (last_fcf) further deducts SBC $13.8M and $0 interest income = $532.2M, tying exactly to reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income. Net debt is a genuine post-acquisition NET DEBT position (not net cash): the $470M debt-funded Leonard Valve acquisition (closed 6 Jan 2026) roughly tripled total debt from $197.3M (FY2025) to $637.5M (30 Jun 2026 10-Q), against $181.3M cash, so no interest-income strip applies (AOS discloses no material interest-income tag; net cash was never > 1x the FCF base even pre-acquisition). Net debt of $456.2M is deducted once in the enterprise-to-equity bridge; interest EXPENSE on the new debt is left inside EBIT/tax as an operating cost of capital structure and is not double-subtracted. Share count: 137.86M is the Q2 2026 (quarter ended 30 Jun 2026) weighted-average DILUTED count from the 10-Q (WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding) -- AOS stopped reporting a dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding cover-page figure after 2015 in this filer's XBRL, so the latest diluted-shares tag is the best available fully-diluted anchor. Held FLAT (annual_share_growth_pct=0) because SBC is fully expensed in the flows -- AOS is a consistent net repurchaser ($400.8M FY2025 buybacks, ~$300M planned FY2026) funding the flat count, so this is a funded convention, not an aspirational one. China segment (~18% of FY2025 sales) is in structural decline (local-currency sales down ~28% YoY in Q2 2026) and under an active strategic review (partnership/restructuring/sale, conclusions expected imminently per Q2 2026 earnings) -- modelled as a drag inside the consolidated growth and margin paths rather than as a separate line, because no segment-level cash flow split is available; the bear case assumes the China drag persists/worsens, the bull case assumes a value-accretive resolution (divestiture or stabilization). Steel cost inflation (~15% FY2026 full-year, ~20% in Q2) and new Section 301 tariffs pressure near-term margin -- modelled as a temporary EBITDA-margin dip in FY2026-27 that recovers as pricing catches up (per management commentary: 'full pricing benefit expected by Q4 2026').

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of revenue_5yr_cagr (5.76%) and equity_5yr_cagr (0.1%), tempered for FY2026 guidance (2-3%) and China structural decline
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (0.1%) diverges sharply from revenue 5yr CAGR (5.76%) and EPS 5yr CAGR (12.67%) -- more than the 30% threshold. This is NOT balance-sheet erosion: AOS has returned essentially all earnings to shareholders via buybacks ($1.4B+ over FY2021-2025) and a growing dividend, holding book equity roughly flat ($1,832M FY2021 -> $1,858M FY2025) while EPS and FCF per share compounded through share-count reduction. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor here (unlike the house default for a growth compounder); revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs are the relevant series. EPS 3yr CAGR (36.6%) is inflated by the FY2022 tariff/inflation trough (EBITDA margin fell to 11.7% from a normal ~20-21%) rebounding in FY2023 -- not a repeatable growth rate; ignored as an anchor for the same reason FCF 3yr CAGR (19.7%) is inflated by the same FY2022 base effect. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (1.56%, OCF-capex-SBC basis, corrected for the CapEx gap described in inputs.notes) is a more reliable reflection of underlying growth than the raw reported FCF figures used before the capex correction.

base.narrative: Base case: FY2026 guidance (2-3% sales growth, narrowed twice on NA residential softness and China weakness) is taken at face value for year 1, with steel/tariff cost inflation (~15% FY2026) compressing EBITDA margin to 19.5% before pricing catches up through H2 2026/2027 and the margin recovers to its recent ~21% normal range by year 4-5. China (~18% of sales, down ~28% local-currency in Q2 2026) continues to shrink through the projection but is assumed to stabilize at a smaller, roughly break-even scale rather than resolve cleanly either way -- the strategic review outcome is treated as noise around the base case, not a discrete event. Leonard Valve ($470M, Jan 2026) contributes its modest revenue and margin-accretive institutional/commercial mix from year 1. Debt taken on for the deal (total debt ~$637.5M vs $197.3M pre-deal) is serviced from FCF with no further leveraging assumed; net debt is a one-time step-change already reflected in the FY0 balance-sheet anchor, not re-modelled through the projection. DOE efficiency-standard transitions (commercial Oct-2026, residential heat-pump mandate phasing to 2029) support a gradual mix-shift to higher-ASP products underpinning the 3-4% mid-decade growth rates before settling to a 3% terminal-adjacent pace reflecting AOS's replacement-cycle-dominated demand base.

bull.narrative: Bull case: the China strategic review concludes with a value-accretive divestiture or partnership that stops the earnings drag and frees management/capital focus, NA residential demand rebounds as housing turnover normalizes and the DOE heat-pump mandate pulls forward replacement-cycle upgrades to higher-ASP units faster than the base case assumes, pricing more than offsets steel/tariff inflation by mid-FY2026 (management's own 'full pricing benefit by Q4' plus some margin recapture), and Leonard Valve becomes a template for further margin-accretive bolt-on M&A in adjacent institutional water-management categories. EBITDA margin expands past its historical ~21% ceiling to 23% on structural mix-shift toward higher-ASP heat-pump/condensing/valve products.

bear.narrative: Bear case: China's decline proves structural rather than cyclical (no resolution from the strategic review, or a value-destructive wind-down), NA residential water heater demand stays soft for longer as new construction and existing-home sales remain depressed through the projection, steel/tariff cost inflation outruns pricing power for an extended period (echoing the FY2022 EBITDA-margin collapse to 11.7%, though not fully repeating it) compressing margin to a 17-19% band versus the historical ~21% norm, and the CFO transition (mid-2026) coincides with execution slippage on the Leonard Valve integration and pricing actions. Elevated post-acquisition leverage (total debt ~3.2x FY2025 level) limits further buyback/M&A flexibility, and WACC is raised 100bp to reflect the thinner margin of safety, consistent with charging risk once in the scenario cash flows and discount rate together rather than double-counting it via an ad-hoc premium on top of an already-weighted scenario.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 guidance taken at face value; steel/tariff margin compression recovers via pricing by 2027; China shrinks but stabilizes; Leonard Valve integrates cleanly; growth settles near AOS's long-run replacement-cycle-driven 3% pace.
scenario_narratives.bull: China review resolves favorably; DOE heat-pump mandate pulls forward higher-ASP replacement demand; pricing outpaces input cost inflation; further accretive bolt-on M&A; margin expands past its historical ceiling.
scenario_narratives.bear: China decline is structural and unresolved; NA residential demand stays soft; steel/tariff inflation outruns pricing for longer; post-acquisition leverage limits flexibility; margin compresses well below the historical norm.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the 15% house default to 25% (bull correspondingly trimmed to 25%) because two live, unresolved negative catalysts sit on top of normal cyclicality: (1) the China segment's outcome is genuinely binary and pending an imminent strategic-review announcement with no visibility yet into terms, and (2) FY2026 guidance has already been cut twice in one year (sales growth 2-4% -> 2-3%, adjusted EPS $3.70-4.00 -> $3.70-3.85), which is evidence the base case itself is already the product of downward revisions, not a stable anchor. This is a going-concern-free, investment-grade industrial, so bear is not raised to distress levels (25%, not 35%+), but the asymmetry of live bad news currently outweighs the case for extra bull optimism.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A. O. Smith is a durable, replacement-demand-dominated North American water heater/boiler/water-treatment manufacturer trading near 52-week lows after two guidance cuts in FY2026, a debt-funded acquisition that tripled leverage, and an unresolved China strategic review. The owner-FCF DCF values the North America core on its historical ~20-21% EBITDA margin and modest mid-single-digit growth, treats the current steel/tariff margin compression as temporary (recovering as pricing catches up per management's own timeline), and treats China as a persistent but bounded drag rather than either a value driver or a write-off. The critical correction in this build is capex: it is NOT present in the parsed XBRL/CSV data (CapEx and FreeCashFlow columns are null for every period), and the automated dcf-context tool's FCF column silently defaulted to raw operating cash flow as a result -- using that figure directly would have overstated owner FCF by the full ~$57-108M/yr capex amount. CapEx was recovered from the non-standard SEC XBRL tag AOS actually uses (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets) and applied consistently across the historical series and the projection.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex was reconstructed from a non-standard XBRL tag rather than read from the parsed CSV/DuckDB -- if AOS later restates or the tag mapping is wrong, the whole FCF base shifts

China strategic review outcome is unresolved and could swing meaningfully positive (accretive divestiture) or negative (disorderly wind-down / continued bleed) versus the base case's assumed stabilization
Post-Leonard-Valve leverage (total debt ~3.2x the FY2025 level) reduces balance-sheet flexibility if end markets stay soft longer than the base case assumes
Steel/tariff cost inflation could persist beyond the assumed FY2026-27 pricing catch-up window, especially if Section 301 tariff policy escalates further
FY2026 guidance has already been cut twice in one year, and management flagged Q3 2026 earnings will be below both Q2 and Q4 -- near-term earnings momentum has visibly stalled
